stops.name: The Counter
stops.intro: Your daily starting point after sign-in.
steps: Start Fresh Catch for ten new or previously missed questions.
Return to your Memory Maki deck, or choose a short Today’s Bento.
Use the sticky bar to check your tier, streak, and achievement collection.

screens.alt: Fresh Catch and Memory Maki are the two main cards on your Counter.
screens.caption: Fresh Catch and Memory Maki are the two main cards on your Counter.

stops.name: Fresh Catch
stops.intro: Choose the subjects and mix for your daily ten.
steps: Select the subjects you want to practice.
Move the unseen-versus-missed slider. The preview shows the actual mix available.
Answer all ten to earn a catch stamp. Wrong answers remain eligible for future catches.

screens.alt: The mix preview adapts when your unseen or missed question pool is short.
screens.caption: The mix preview adapts when your unseen or missed question pool is short.

stops.name: Memory Maki
stops.intro: Answer, learn from the feedback, then rate your familiarity.
steps: Build a deck from selected subjects, topics, and a question range.
Answer the question to reveal its explanation immediately.
Rate familiarity from 1 to 5. Lower ratings return more often during the session.
Track the colored rating bar. At 80% rated 5, you can finish, keep rolling, or take a recall check.

screens.alt: The colored bar shows how many questions are unrated or rated 1 through 5.
screens.caption: The colored bar shows how many questions are unrated or rated 1 through 5.

screens.alt: After reading the feedback, choose how well you know the question.
screens.caption: After reading the feedback, choose how well you know the question.

stops.name: Mentor and Rush
stops.intro: Choose immediate teaching or a timed challenge.
steps: Maki Mentor checks each answer and provides feedback during the round.
Wasabi Rush uses a timer and reveals feedback after submission.
Both use the same three-step setup: coverage, round settings, and review.

screens.alt: Maki Mentor uses a guided setup with a live count of matching questions.
screens.caption: Maki Mentor uses a guided setup with a live count of matching questions.

screens.alt: Wasabi Rush adds a time limit before you start the challenge.
screens.caption: Wasabi Rush adds a time limit before you start the challenge.

stops.name: Roll Call
stops.intro: Browse the bank and choose exactly what to study.
steps: Search by text or question ID and narrow the subject.
Switch among all, unseen, missed, and saved questions.
Add questions to the study tray, then start a practice round or Memory Maki deck.
Use private notes for your reasoning or report a question for Head Chef to review.

screens.alt: Roll Call combines search, saved questions, and a study tray.
screens.caption: Roll Call combines search, saved questions, and a study tray.

stops.name: Bento Builder
stops.intro: Create a reviewed exam and downloadable PDF set.
steps: Choose coverage or load a saved class recipe.
Allocate questions evenly, by subject count, or by topic and difficulty quotas.
Preview the actual questions and replace any item before saving.
Save the bento, then prepare the exam paper, answer sheet, and answer key PDFs.

screens.alt: Quota rows let you set an exact count for each subject, topic, and difficulty.
screens.caption: Quota rows let you set an exact count for each subject, topic, and difficulty.

stops.name: Progress and crew
stops.intro: See your learning patterns and collect your sushi crew.
steps: My Progress shows coverage and accuracy, with subject and time filters.
Memory Maki answers contribute to unique completion as soon as you answer.
Your Passport lists achievement requirements. Earn characters and equip them in your profile.
Every 200 unique completed questions earns a tier; the leaderboard counts weekly practice under its repeat rules.

screens.alt: Your progress view keeps subject coverage and accuracy visible.
screens.caption: Your progress view keeps subject coverage and accuracy visible.

screens.alt: Achievement cards show their character, requirement, and earned status.
screens.caption: Achievement cards show their character, requirement, and earned status.

stops.name: Head Chef
stops.intro: Manage learners, class practice, and the question bank.
steps: Open Head Chef from your account menu whenever you need the administrator tools.
Add learners individually or preview a CSV roster to create invitation links.
Use the quality queue to review questions and preserve corrections as new versions.
Share class recipes, assign saved exams, and inspect cohort progress or backup status.

screens.alt: Head Chef tools are grouped above the learner list. This screenshot uses demo accounts.
screens.caption: Head Chef tools are grouped above the learner list. This screenshot uses demo accounts.
